family_title: Gap fill 3: interpolation, output-space arithmetic, federated LoRA, head-only and memory-lean tuning, discrete prompts

methods.name: Concept Sliders
methods.full_name: Concept Sliders (attribute-direction LoRA with a continuous inference-time strength)
methods.paper_title: Concept Sliders: LoRA Adaptors for Precise Control in Diffusion Models
methods.formula_latex: W(\alpha)=W_0+\alpha\,BA,\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \alpha\in\mathbb{R}\ \text{(slider strength, set at inference)};\ \ \text{text sliders regress the slider model onto the frozen model's guided score: }\epsilon_{\theta^{*}}(X,c_t,t)\leftarrow\epsilon_{\theta}(X,c_t,t)+\eta\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\big(\epsilon_{\theta}(X,(c_{+},p),t)-\epsilon_{\theta}(X,(c_{-},p),t)\big);\ \ \text{image-pair sliders: }\min_{A,B}\|\epsilon_{\theta_{-}}(x^{A}_t,\varnothing,t)-\epsilon\|^2+\|\epsilon_{\theta_{+}}(x^{B}_t,\varnothing,t)-\epsilon\|^2\ (\theta_{\pm}:\ \alpha=\pm1);\ \ \text{composition: }W=W_0+\sum_k\alpha_kB_kA_k;\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix per slider (default } r=4\text{)}
methods.locus: LoRA on the diffusion U-Net (SD-XL, SD-1.4); the official text-slider config adapts all layers except cross-attention ('noxattn'), including 3x3 conv layers ('c3lier'), with rank 4 and alpha 1, so the code applies the fixed internal scale alpha/r = 1/4 times the slider multiplier; at inference the slider is switched on only after the first t denoising steps (SDEdit-style)
methods.structure: Each slider is a rank-r ray \{W_0+\alpha BA:\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\} through W_0, i.e. a one-parameter additive family in weight space; K sliders span the affine slice W_0+\mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{B_kA_k\}_{k=1}^{K}, navigated by the coefficient vector (\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_K). The training target is an output-space (score) contrast \epsilon(c_+)-\epsilon(c_-) distilled into this weight direction.
methods.mergeable_reason: For any fixed strength vector the update \sum_k \alpha_k B_k A_k is a plain matrix that folds into W_0; the SDEdit-style schedule only switches between W_0 and the merged weights across denoising steps.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B = 0); in addition, alpha = 0 recovers the base model exactly at any time after training, since every slider is a ray through W_0.
methods.key_idea: Train a LoRA whose direction encodes a single attribute, using the frozen model's own guidance-style score difference between opposing prompts (with preservation prompts to disentangle) or before/after image pairs as the target; scaling the LoRA multiplier then dials the attribute continuously up or down, and sliders add.
methods.results_note: On SD-XL, a 'fix hands' slider cut the rater-judged rate of distorted hands from 62% to 22%, the disentanglement objective lowered attribute interference from 0.36 to 0.10, and up to 50 sliders were composed in one model.

relations.note: architecturally each slider is a LoRA whose multiplier alpha is exposed as a continuous control
composing sliders, W_0 + sum_k alpha_k B_k A_k, is task arithmetic with low-rank task vectors and user-chosen signed coefficients
sliders distil an output-space contrast eps(c+) - eps(c-) into a weight-space direction; proxy-tuning applies an output-space (logit) contrast at decode time without touching weights
both combine several diffusion LoRAs; ZipLoRA learns per-column merge coefficients instead of exposing user-set scalar strengths
alternative way to apply several diffusion LoRAs at once (switching/compositing across denoising steps)

corrections: locus: added the official config's rank 4 / alpha 1 (internal scale alpha/r = 1/4 multiplying the slider strength) and the 'c3lier' conv-layer coverage, from trainscripts/textsliders/data/config.yaml and lora.py
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2311.12092 (Gandikota, 2023-11) confirmed; ECCV 2024 confirmed via Crossref (LNCS, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-73661-2_10) and Semantic Scholar. Eqs. 4, 7, 8, 9 of the paper match the formula (W = W_0 + alpha*DeltaW with alpha set at inference; disentanglement target; image-pair loss with theta_+/theta_-). Code (lora.py) inits lora_up to zeros, so B = 0 at init. 62% -> 22% distorted hands, interference 0.36 -> 0.10 (Table 3, age slider) and 50-slider composition confirmed. Not in HF PEFT as a training method (peft.helpers.rescale_adapter_scale or add_weighted_adapter can set strengths/compose trained sliders, but the guided-score objective is absent).

methods.name: IC-LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\ \text{in the FLUX.1-dev DiT},\ r=\alpha=16\ \text{(official config)};\ \ \text{training input: one composite image }X=[\,x_1\,|\,x_2\,|\cdots|\,x_n\,]\ \text{(n panels concatenated spatially) with one merged caption }c=[c_{\text{set}};c_1;\dots;c_n];\ \ \text{loss: the base model's own flow-matching objective on }(X,c);\ \ \text{image-conditioned use: mask some panels and inpaint them from the rest with SDEdit (training-free)};\ W_0\ \text{and text encoders frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained on 20--100 image sets per task}
methods.locus: LoRA on the layers of a text-to-image diffusion transformer (FLUX.1-dev); the task itself is carried by the input format (panel-concatenated image + merged prompt), not by new modules
methods.structure: Plain low-rank \Delta W=BA; the cross-image conditioning is supplied by the DiT's existing full self-attention over the tokens of all panels in one canvas, so the adapter only re-weights an in-context capability the base model already has (no token-routing masks, no extra encoders).
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter is a standard LoRA on an unchanged DiT, so BA folds into W_0; the multi-panel behaviour comes from the input canvas and prompt.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B = 0) on an unmodified architecture, so the zero adapter is exactly FLUX.1-dev.
methods.key_idea: Text-to-image DiTs can already draw coherent multi-panel images from one merged prompt; concatenating image sets into a single canvas with a joint caption and training a small task-specific LoRA on 20-100 examples activates this in-context ability, and SDEdit-style masking turns it into reference-conditioned generation.
methods.results_note: Qualitative results only: storyboards, font design, portrait photography, home decoration, visual identity and visual effects, each trained for 5,000 steps (batch 4, rank 16) on one A100; no quantitative benchmark is reported.

relations.note: the trainable object is an ordinary LoRA; the contribution is the data/input recipe
both reuse the DiT's own attention over concatenated image tokens; OminiControl concatenates condition tokens in sequence and adds an attention bias, IC-LoRA concatenates panels in pixel space
alternative LoRA-based conditioning of DiTs on reference images

corrections: formula_latex: alpha fixed to 16 (linear_alpha in config/movie-shots.yml, so alpha/r = 1); 'denoising objective' replaced by the flow-matching objective actually used (noise_scheduler: flowmatch); text encoders marked frozen (train_text_encoder: false)
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.23775 (Lianghua Huang, 2024-10; comment 'Tech report') confirmed; no peer-reviewed venue found (Semantic Scholar lists arXiv only), so venue stays arXiv. Method section confirms image concatenation, merged prompts, LoRA on 20-100 sets, SDEdit for conditioning; implementation details (FLUX.1-dev, 5,000 steps, batch 4, rank 16, one A100) and 'qualitative only' confirmed. Official ai-toolkit config: lora linear 16 / linear_alpha 16, flowmatch, text encoder frozen. Not in HF PEFT as a method (the resulting weights are plain LoRA).

methods.name: Proxy-Tuning
methods.full_name: Proxy-tuning (decoding-time tuning of a large model through a small tuned/untuned pair)
methods.formula_latex: p_{\tilde{\mathcal M}}(X_t\mid x_{<t})=\mathrm{softmax}\big[s_{\mathcal M}(X_t\mid x_{<t})+s_{\mathcal M^{+}}(X_t\mid x_{<t})-s_{\mathcal M^{-}}(X_t\mid x_{<t})\big];\ \ \mathcal M:\ \text{large base model (frozen; only its logits are used)},\ \mathcal M^{-}:\ \text{small base model (frozen)},\ \mathcal M^{+}:\ \mathcal M^{-}\ \text{after tuning};\ \text{models must share a vocabulary}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{in }\mathcal M;\ \text{only the small proxy }\mathcal M^{-}\to\mathcal M^{+}\ \text{is tuned (any method, done once)}
methods.locus: next-token logits at decoding time; the large model's weights are never accessed
methods.structure: Output-space (logit) arithmetic: the large model's logit vector is translated by the small model's tuning vector s_{\mathcal M^{+}}-s_{\mathcal M^{-}}, i.e. task arithmetic in logit space, equivalently a product of experts \propto p_{\mathcal M}\,p_{\mathcal M^{+}}/p_{\mathcal M^{-}} with one expert and one anti-expert (DExperts).
methods.mergeable_reason: Every decoding step needs forward passes of three models; nothing is folded into the large model's weights.
methods.identity_at_init: If the proxy is untuned (M+ = M-), the offset vanishes and the large model's distribution is recovered exactly.
methods.key_idea: Tune a small model, then add the difference between its tuned and untuned logits to a large (possibly black-box) model's logits at each decoding step, transferring the effect of tuning without touching the large model's weights.
methods.results_note: Steering Llama2-13B and 70B base with Llama2-7B chat/base proxies closed 91.1% and 88.1% of the gap to the true chat models on average over five settings (AlpacaFarm, GSM, ToxiGen, TruthfulQA multiple-choice and open-ended); it was also applied to GPT-3.5 using only its top-5 log-probabilities (+2.3% on RealTimeQA).

relations.note: the per-token EFT up-scaling rule pi_ref^N * pi^M / pi_ref^M normalizes to the same softmax of s_M + s_{M+} - s_{M-}; the two papers are concurrent
adds a 'tuning vector' in logit space instead of in weight space
both adapt a model whose weights are inaccessible; BBT searches a soft prompt gradient-free, proxy-tuning needs output logits but no prompt optimization
the paper's appendix compares proxy-tuning with LoRA for task fine-tuning

corrections: results_note: clarified that the 91.1%/88.1% averages are over five settings (TruthfulQA counted as MC and open-ended) and added the +2.3% RealTimeQA gain for GPT-3.5
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2401.08565 (Alisa Liu, 2024-01; comment 'COLM 2024 camera-ready') confirmed. Eq. in Sec. 2 is exactly softmax[s_M + s_M+ - s_M-] with a shared-vocabulary requirement; Sec. 8 states that Mitchell et al. (EFT) apply 'the same DExperts equation', justifying equivalent-to; Appendix D compares with LoRA. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: EFT
methods.paper_title: An Emulator for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models using Small Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \pi^{N}_{M}(y\mid x)\propto\pi^{N}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)\,\frac{\pi^{M}(y\mid x)}{\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)}=\pi^{N}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)\exp\big(r^{M}_{\pi}(x,y)\big),\ \ r^{M}_{\pi}=\log\tfrac{\pi^{M}}{\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}}};\ \ \text{sampled per token: }\tilde\pi(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})=\tfrac{1}{Z(x,y_{<t})}\pi^{N}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})\tfrac{\pi^{M}(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})}{\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_t\mid x,y_{<t})};\ \ \text{up-scaling: }N>M\ \text{(large base, small fine-tuned and small base)};\ \text{all models frozen}
methods.structure: Reward transport across scales: fine-tuning is viewed as KL-regularized RL, so a fine-tuned model equals its base times \exp(\text{implicit reward}); EFT moves the small-scale implicit reward \log(\pi^{M}/\pi^{M}_{\mathrm{ref}}) onto a large-scale base, a log-linear (logit-additive) composition of three models.
methods.mergeable_reason: Sampling requires the large base and both small models at every step (speculative decoding reduces but does not remove this cost).
methods.identity_at_init: Setting N = M returns the original fine-tuned policy; an untuned small model (pi^M = pi^M_ref) returns the large base model.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning's effect can be isolated as the log-ratio between a fine-tuned model and its base; adding a small model's log-ratio to a large base model emulates fine-tuning the large model, and decouples the scales of pre-training and fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Averaged over Llama-1, Llama-2 and Falcon on Anthropic-HH and ELI5, up-scaling recovered nearly 70% of the factuality gain of the truly fine-tuned large model (scores normalized so that the small fine-tuned model is 0 and the large fine-tuned model is 1); speculative EFT decoding sped up sampling by nearly 2.5x when up-scaling Llama-2-7B-chat with Llama-2-70B-base.

relations.note: concurrent work with the same per-token logit-arithmetic rule; EFT gives the KL-regularized-RL derivation
transports a fine-tuning delta in log-probability space rather than weight space

corrections: results_note: made the normalization behind 'nearly 70%' explicit (0 = small fine-tuned, 1 = large fine-tuned), as in Fig. 3
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2310.12962 (Mitchell, 2023-10) confirmed; ICLR 2024 (poster) confirmed via OpenReview (venueid ICLR.cc/2024/Conference). Eqs. 3-5 match the formula, including the per-timestep partition function and 'N = M corresponds to sampling from the original policy'. No official code found. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: WiSE-FT
methods.hf_peft_config: peft.helpers.rescale_adapter_scale(model, multiplier=alpha) with alpha in [0,1]: LoRA-adapter form only (scales Delta W toward W_0, which the PEFT docstring calls strictly equivalent to WiSE-FT); heads trained via modules_to_save are not interpolated
methods.formula_latex: \theta_{\alpha}=(1-\alpha)\,\theta_0+\alpha\,\theta_1=\theta_0+\alpha(\theta_1-\theta_0),\ \ \alpha\in[0,1];\ \ \theta_0=[V_{\mathrm{enc}},W_{\text{zero-shot}}]\ \text{(zero-shot CLIP: pre-trained encoder + text-derived head)},\ \theta_1=\text{standard (end-to-end or head-only) fine-tuned weights};\ \ \text{per matrix: }W=W_0+\alpha\,\Delta W;\ \text{only }\alpha\ \text{is chosen post hoc (default }0.5\text{)}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{beyond the underlying fine-tuning (which updates all parameters); one scalar }\alpha
methods.locus: all parameters of the image encoder and the classification head
methods.structure: The segment \{\theta_0+\alpha(\theta_1-\theta_0)\}_{\alpha\in[0,1]} joining the pre-trained point and the fine-tuned point in weight space (a two-point convex combination); when only the linear head is fine-tuned it coincides with the output-space ensemble (1-\alpha)f(x,\theta_0)+\alpha f(x,\theta_1).
methods.mergeable_reason: The interpolated weights form a single model of the original architecture, so inference costs exactly one model.
methods.identity_at_init: alpha = 0 returns the zero-shot model and alpha = 1 the fine-tuned one; for end-to-end fine-tuning the head is initialized with the (temperature-scaled) zero-shot classifier.
methods.key_idea: Zero-shot CLIP is robust under distribution shift while fine-tuning is accurate in distribution; because the two endpoints are linearly connected in weight space, simply interpolating their weights keeps most of both at no extra inference cost.
methods.results_note: On ImageNet and five derived distribution shifts with CLIP, WiSE-FT improved accuracy under shift by 4-6 pp over prior work while raising ImageNet accuracy by 1.6 pp.

relations.note: WiSE-FT is task arithmetic with a single task vector tau = theta_1 - theta_0 and lambda = alpha in [0,1]
same group's follow-up averages several fine-tuned endpoints instead of interpolating back toward the zero-shot start
concurrent robust fine-tuning recipe addressing the same ID/OOD trade-off by initialization rather than interpolation
with head-only fine-tuning, WiSE-FT returns the linear probe at alpha = 1 (warm-started from the zero-shot head) and the output ensemble of the zero-shot head and the probe for 0 < alpha < 1

corrections: hf_peft: false -> true; PEFT main (85be3f3, v0.21.1) ships peft.helpers.rescale_adapter_scale, documented as strictly equivalent to WiSE-FT for LoRA with multiplier in [0,1]
hf_peft_config: added the helper call and its scope (LoRA layers only)
relations[linear-probing].note: restated precisely (alpha = 1 endpoint is the probe; intermediate alpha is an output ensemble)
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2109.01903 (Wortsman, 2021-09; comment 'CVPR 2022') confirmed. Eq. 1 wse(x, alpha) = f(x, (1-alpha) theta_0 + alpha theta_1) and the linear-classifier equivalence to an output-space ensemble confirmed; alpha = 0.5 recommended; head initialized with the temperature-scaled zero-shot classifier for end-to-end fine-tuning (App. D). 4-6 pp OOD and +1.6 pp ImageNet confirmed from the abstract.

methods.name: Linear probing
methods.full_name: Linear probing (head-only tuning on frozen pre-trained features)
methods.paper_title: DeCAF: A Deep Convolutional Activation Feature for Generic Visual Recognition
methods.formula_latex: f(x)=V^{\top}g_{B_0}(x)\ (+\,b),\ \ B_0\ \text{(entire pre-trained backbone) frozen},\ \ V\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times K}\ \text{new linear head, trained by }\min_{V}\sum_i\ell\big(V^{\top}g_{B_0}(x_i),y_i\big)+\lambda\|V\|^2\ \text{(convex: logistic regression or linear SVM)}
methods.trainable_params: dK\ (+K)\ \text{for }d\text{-dim features and }K\text{ classes; nothing inside the backbone}
methods.locus: a new final linear classifier on top of frozen penultimate (or intermediate) features
methods.structure: The trivial selection: the trainable coordinate set is exactly the task head, so the backbone map g_{B_0} is held fixed (the identity on the backbone factor of parameter space); any PEFT method that also trains the head contains linear probing as its restriction to \Delta(\text{backbone})=0.
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the task head is learned and the backbone is untouched, so inference is the original network plus the head that any fine-tuning would need.
methods.identity_at_init: The backbone function is preserved exactly throughout; the head is new (random or zero initialized), so there is no pre-trained output to preserve.
methods.key_idea: Reuse a frozen pre-trained representation and fit only a linear classifier on it; the problem is convex and cheap and keeps the features intact (good out-of-distribution extrapolation), but it cannot adapt the features to the task.
methods.results_note: In DeCAF, a linear SVM on frozen DeCAF6 features (trained with dropout) reached 86.9% mean per-class accuracy on Caltech-101 with 30 images per class, 2.6 points above the prior multi-kernel state of the art (84.3%); Kumar et al. (2022) later found linear probing about 7 points better out of distribution than full fine-tuning on 10 shift datasets (66.2% vs 59.3%).

relations.note: bias-only tuning plus the head reduces to linear probing when the bias update is zero
LP-FT uses the linear-probing optimum as the head initialization of full fine-tuning
surgical fine-tuning's block choices include the final linear layer ('Last Layer'); selecting only that block is exactly linear probing

corrections: results_note: specified the dropout-trained SVM on DeCAF6, the prior SOTA (84.3%, +2.6 points) and the exact LP/FT OOD averages (66.2% vs 59.3%)
relations[surgical-fine-tuning].note: replaced the vague 'mild extension' with the exact reduction (Lee et al. list 'Last Layer' among the tunable blocks)
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 1310.1531 (Donahue, 2013-10) confirmed; ICML 2014 confirmed via PMLR v32 (donahue14). DeCAF Fig. 4/Sec. 4.1 confirm LogReg/SVM on frozen DeCAF5-7 features and 86.91 +- 0.7 for SVM+dropout on DeCAF6. Attribution of 'linear probing' to DeCAF is a canonical-example choice (no single originating paper). LP-FT figures checked in arXiv 2202.10054. Not in HF PEFT as a method (modules_to_save trains a head but is not a probe config).

methods.name: LP-FT
methods.paper_title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution
methods.formula_latex: f_{v,B}(x)=v^{\top}g_B(x);\ \ \text{stage 1 (LP): }v_{\mathrm{lp}}=\arg\min_{v}\widehat L(v,B_0)\ \text{with }B=B_0\ \text{frozen};\ \ \text{stage 2 (FT): gradient descent on }\widehat L(v,B)\ \text{over all of }(v,B)\ \text{starting from }(v_{\mathrm{lp}},B_0)
methods.locus: first the linear head only, then every layer
methods.structure: A two-stage training schedule: the head-only (selective) optimum initializes full fine-tuning, which shrinks the head-alignment error \varphi^2=|(v_0^{\top}v_\star)^2-(v_\star^{\top}v_\star)^2| that otherwise drives large, ID-only feature updates; in the two-layer linear theory, features in directions outside the training span are then not distorted.
methods.mergeable_reason: The output is a single fine-tuned network of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Stage 2 starts at the pre-trained backbone B_0 with the linear-probing head v_lp instead of a random head, i.e. at the best frozen-feature predictor.
methods.key_idea: With a random head, full fine-tuning distorts pretrained features: gradients from the badly aligned head change the features of in-distribution directions while out-of-distribution directions stay put. Fitting the head by linear probing first removes most of this coupling, so the method gets fine-tuning's in-distribution accuracy and linear probing's robustness.
methods.results_note: Across 10 distribution-shift datasets, LP-FT was about 1% better in distribution and 10% better out of distribution than full fine-tuning, and changed features 10-100x less than fine-tuning.

relations.note: stage 1 is linear probing
concurrent robust fine-tuning recipe (interpolation instead of initialization)
another selective remedy for fine-tuning under distribution shift

corrections: structure: added the absolute value in the head-alignment error phi^2 = |(v_0^T v*)^2 - (v*^T v*)^2| as defined in Theorem 3.3
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2202.10054 (Kumar, 2022-02; comment 'ICLR (Oral) 2022') confirmed. Stage-wise formula, 1% ID / 10% OOD gains over FT on 10 shift datasets and the 10x-100x smaller feature change confirmed in the text. Code repo AnanyaKumar/transfer_learning resolves. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: FFA-LoRA
methods.paper_title: Improving LoRA in Privacy-preserving Federated Learning
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+BA_0,\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained (init }0),\ A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{random Gaussian, frozen and shared by all clients};\ \ \text{FedAvg: }B^{+}=\textstyle\sum_kp_kB_k\Rightarrow W_0+B^{+}A_0=W_0+\sum_kp_kB_kA_0\ \text{(exact average of client updates, unlike }(\sum_kp_kB_k)(\sum_kp_kA_k));\ \ \text{DP-SGD noise enters only as }\xi_BA_0
methods.locus: standard LoRA sites (attention and feed-forward linear layers in the RoBERTa experiments)
methods.structure: \Delta W ranges over the linear subspace \{BA_0:B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\} with a fixed random row space, so \Delta W is linear in the trainable parameters and client aggregation commutes with the parametrization (no cross terms B_iA_j, no quadratic noise term \xi_B\xi_A).
methods.mergeable_reason: BA_0 is an ordinary matrix that folds into W_0 exactly as in LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0, so Delta W = 0; A_0 is random Gaussian and never trained; the scaling factor alpha becomes unnecessary (the paper shows LoRA's trajectory tends to FFA-LoRA's as alpha goes to infinity).
methods.key_idea: LoRA's bilinear BA breaks federated averaging (the average of products is not the product of averages) and amplifies differential-privacy noise; freezing the random A makes the update linear in B, so FedAvg is exact, DP noise is not squared, and communication is halved.
methods.results_note: In a 3-client heterogeneous federated setting with RoBERTa-Large, FFA-LoRA beat LoRA on GLUE tasks with and without DP (e.g. MNLI-m 78.8% vs 39.5% at epsilon = 6), and reached 17.12% vs 15.68% on GSM-8K with LLaMA-7B.

relations.note: identical parametrization to LoRA-FA v1 (frozen random A, trainable zero-initialized B); LoRA-FA is motivated by activation memory and its current version adds a projected B-gradient, FFA-LoRA by exact federated aggregation and DP
same train-B / freeze-random-A design (AsyLoRA samples A with orthonormal rows rather than Gaussian), there justified by generalization bounds
LoRA with A fixed at its random initialization
both remove LoRA's FedAvg aggregation error (cross terms B_iA_j); FLoRA keeps A trainable and stacks client modules instead (the FLoRA paper does not compare against FFA-LoRA directly)

corrections: relations[lora-fa]: equivalent-to -> competes-with; the catalog's LoRA-FA entry includes a projected-gradient optimizer FFA-LoRA does not use (lora-fa and asylora are already linked by competes-with)
relations[asylora]: equivalent-to -> competes-with; AsyLoRA's frozen A has orthonormal rows, FFA-LoRA's is Gaussian
relations[flora-federated].note: noted that the FLoRA paper does not benchmark FFA-LoRA
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2403.12313 (Youbang Sun, 2024-03; comment 'published at ICLR 2024') confirmed. Sec. 4: W = W_0 + B A_0 with A_0 Gaussian and frozen, B_0 = 0; DP noise only in xi_B A; LoRA tends to FFA-LoRA as alpha -> infinity (Theorem). 3-client RoBERTa-Large setup, MNLI-m 78.81 vs 39.46 at eps = 6 (Table 1) and GSM-8K 17.12% vs 15.68% with LLaMA-7B confirmed. No official code found. Not in HF PEFT (freezing lora_A by hand emulates it; PEFT's LoRA-FA optimizer adds a gradient projection).

methods.name: FLoRA (federated)
methods.full_name: FLoRA: stacking-based federated fine-tuning with heterogeneous LoRA ranks
methods.paper_title: FLoRA: Federated Fine-Tuning Large Language Models with Heterogeneous Low-Rank Adaptations
methods.formula_latex: \text{client }k:\ W_0+B_kA_k,\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r_k},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times d_{in}}\ \text{(heterogeneous }r_k,\ \text{re-initialized every round)};\ \ \text{server: }A=p_1A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus p_KA_K\in\mathbb{R}^{(\sum_kr_k)\times d_{in}}\ \text{(row stacking)},\ B=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_K\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times\sum_kr_k}\ \text{(column stacking)};\ \ BA=\textstyle\sum_kp_kB_kA_k,\ \ p_k=|D_k|/\sum_j|D_j|;\ \ \text{clients then update }W_0\leftarrow W_0+BA
methods.trainable_params: r_k(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{on client }k;\ \text{the broadcast global module has }(\textstyle\sum_kr_k)(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{entries}
methods.locus: LoRA on the self-attention layers only (following the original LoRA paper) of TinyLlama-1.1B, Llama-7B and Llama2-7B
methods.structure: Direct sum of the clients' rank spaces \mathbb{R}^{r_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathbb{R}^{r_K}: block concatenation of factors satisfies [B_1\cdots B_K][A_1;\dots;A_K]=\sum_kB_kA_k exactly, so the aggregate factors through \sum_kr_k dimensions with no cross terms B_iA_j (which FedAvg of A and B separately introduces) and with no constraint that ranks agree.
methods.mergeable_reason: After each round the aggregated BA is added into the base weights, so the final model is the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Clients re-initialize their local LoRA each round (the official code uses PEFT's LoraConfig, i.e. B = 0), so each round starts exactly at the current global model.
methods.key_idea: Averaging LoRA's A and B separately does not average the products; stacking the client factors instead gives the exact weighted sum of updates and naturally supports clients with different ranks.
methods.results_note: On MMLU and MT-bench with TinyLlama, Llama and Llama2 fine-tuned federatedly on Dolly, Alpaca, Wizard and ShareGPT, FLoRA outperformed FedIT in homogeneous settings and zero-padding in heterogeneous-rank settings (zero-padded FedIT dropped to 7.97% MMLU for Llama on Alpaca).

relations.note: alternative cure for LoRA's FedAvg aggregation error (freeze A vs stack factors)
both support heterogeneous client ranks; HetLoRA zero-pads and averages factors with norm-based weights
uses the same block-stacking identity sum_k B_k A_k = [B_1 ... B_K][A_1; ...; A_K], with data-size weights instead of learned per-layer coefficients
client modules are standard LoRA

corrections: code_url: github.com/ATP-1010/FederatedLLM now 301-redirects to github.com/ziyaow1010/FederatedLLM; updated to the canonical location
locus: restricted to self-attention layers, as stated in Sec. 4.1, and gave model sizes
identity_at_init: grounded the B = 0 claim in the official code (PEFT LoraConfig); the paper only says modules are re-initialized each round
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2409.05976 (Ziyao Wang, 2024-09) confirmed; NeurIPS 2024 confirmed via the NeurIPS proceedings listing. Eqs. 9-12: A = p_0A_0 (+) ... (+) p_KA_K (rows), B = B_0 (+) ... (+) B_K (columns), p_k applied to one factor only, per-round re-initialization confirmed. Baselines are FedIT and zero-padding (citing HetLoRA's workshop version), not FFA-LoRA; 7.97% MMLU (Llama, Alpaca, zero-padding) confirmed. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: HetLoRA
methods.paper_title: Heterogeneous LoRA for Federated Fine-tuning of On-Device Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: \text{distribute by truncation: }B_k^{(t,0)}=\overline B^{(t)}_{:,:r_k},\ A_k^{(t,0)}=\overline A^{(t)}_{:r_k,:};\ \ \text{local: }\min_{B_k,A_k}\ \ell(B_k,A_k\mid W_0)+\lambda\,\|B_{k,:,\gamma r_k:r_k}\|\,\|A_{k,\gamma r_k:r_k,:}\|\ (\gamma<1,\ \text{rank self-pruning});\ \ \text{server (zero-pad to }r_{\max}):\ \overline B^{(t+1)}=\textstyle\sum_kp_kB_k,\ \overline A^{(t+1)}=\sum_kp_kA_k,\ \ p_k\propto\|B_kA_k\|_F;\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.locus: LoRA on the self-attention layers only (following the original LoRA paper) of on-device PaLM 2 XXS and XS
methods.structure: Nested rank truncations: client k sees the leading r_k columns of B and rows of A of a global rank-r_{\max} pair; aggregation zero-pads and averages factors separately with weights proportional to \|B_kA_k\|_F (so cross terms remain), and a tail-norm penalty lets clients shrink r_k.
methods.mergeable_reason: The final global pair BA is a plain low-rank matrix that folds into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the paper; clients receive truncations of the current global LoRA pair, so with LoRA's standard B = 0 initialization the first round starts exactly at W_0.
methods.key_idea: Let resource-limited clients train smaller-rank slices of one global LoRA, prune unnecessary rank locally, and weight the server average toward clients whose updates carry more signal.
methods.results_note: With PaLM 2 XXS/XS on multi-session chat (perplexity) and Reddit summarization (RougeL), HetLoRA beat homogeneous-rank LoRA and a reconstruct-then-SVD baseline, slightly below full federated fine-tuning.

relations.note: FLoRA replaces zero-padded factor averaging with exact factor stacking
client modules are truncations of one LoRA

corrections: identity_at_init: the paper does not state the global initialization; reworded as conditional on LoRA's standard B = 0
locus: restricted to self-attention layers, as stated in Sec. 4

relations: removed hetlora -> adalora (competes-with); neither paper compares against or cites the other, and the settings (federated tail-norm self-pruning vs centralized SVD-triplet budget allocation) differ
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2401.06432 (Yae Jee Cho, 2024-01) confirmed; EMNLP 2024 main confirmed via ACL Anthology 2024.emnlp-main.717. Truncation B_{:,:r_k}, A_{:r_k,:}, the tail-norm regularizer with gamma < 1, zero-padding and p_k = ||S_k||/Z with ||S_k|| computed as ||B_kA_k||_F confirmed (Sec. 3.3). Table 3 confirms HetLoRA > HomLoRA and Recon+SVD, slightly below full FT. No official code found. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: TinyTL
methods.full_name: Tiny Transfer Learning (bias tuning with lite residual modules)
methods.paper_title: TinyTL: Reduce Memory, Not Parameters for Efficient On-Device Learning
methods.formula_latex: a_{i+1}=\mathcal F_{W}(a_i)+b+\mathcal F_{w_r}\big(a_i'\big),\ \ a_i'=\mathrm{reduce}(a_i)\ \text{(}2\times2\ \text{average pooling)};\ \ W\ \text{frozen (8-bit)},\ \text{trained: biases }b,\ \text{lite residual weights }w_r\ \text{(group convolution, no }1\times1\ \text{expansion, output bilinearly upsampled), classifier head};\ \ \text{rationale: }\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial W}=a_i^{\top}\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial a_{i+1}}\ \text{needs the stored activation }a_i,\ \tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial b}=\tfrac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial a_{i+1}}\ \text{does not}
methods.locus: all bias vectors, one lite residual branch per mobile inverted-bottleneck block, and the classifier head (BatchNorm replaced by GroupNorm)
methods.structure: Selective translation of every layer's output (bias shift) plus a parallel low-resolution, narrow residual branch (downsample, group conv, upsample) per block; chosen to minimize stored activations rather than parameter count.
methods.mergeable_reason: Bias updates fold in trivially, but the lite residual branches are extra nonlinear modules that stay at inference (in the default protocol they are already part of the pre-trained architecture).
methods.identity_at_init: By default the lite residual modules are present during pre-training and initialized from those weights, so transfer starts exactly at the pre-trained function; with randomly initialized lite residuals (TinyTL-RandomL+B) there is no such guarantee and accuracy drops.
methods.key_idea: On-device training memory is dominated by the activations needed for weight gradients, not by the parameter count; bias gradients need no stored activations, so freeze weights, train biases, and recover capacity with tiny residual branches whose activations are small.
methods.results_note: TinyTL saved up to 6.5x training memory relative to full fine-tuning with little accuracy loss, was up to 34.1% more accurate than last-layer tuning, and with feature-extractor adaptation saved 7.3-12.9x memory without accuracy loss.

relations.note: the TinyTL-B variant (biases + head) is bias-only tuning; TinyTL adds lite residual modules
last-layer tuning (FT-Last) is the paper's baseline and the restriction of TinyTL to the head
both target activation memory rather than parameter count; LST moves the trainable path to a side network
parallel convolutional residual adapters for vision transfer

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2007.11622 (Han Cai, 2020-07; comment 'NeurIPS 2020') confirmed; the NeurIPS 2020 proceedings title 'TinyTL: Reduce Memory, Not Parameters for Efficient On-Device Learning' is confirmed (arXiv title differs). Eq. 4 a_{i+1} = F_W(a_i) + b + F_{w_r}(reduce(a_i)), 2x2 average pooling, group conv without 1x1 projection, bilinear upsampling, GN instead of BN, 8-bit frozen weights and pre-trained lite-residual initialization (Table 4) confirmed. 6.5x / 34.1% / 7.3-12.9x are the abstract's figures (Sec. 4 text gives 7.5-12.9x). Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: AutoPrompt
methods.paper_title: AutoPrompt: Eliciting Knowledge from Language Models with Automatically Generated Prompts
methods.formula_latex: x_{\text{prompt}}=\lambda(x_{\text{inp}},x_{\text{trig}}),\ \ x_{\text{trig}}=(x^{(1)}_{\text{trig}},\dots,x^{(\ell)}_{\text{trig}})\in\mathcal V^{\ell}\ \text{(discrete tokens shared across inputs, initialized to [MASK])};\ \ p(y\mid x_{\text{prompt}})=\textstyle\sum_{w\in\mathcal V_y}p([\mathrm{MASK}]=w\mid x_{\text{prompt}});\ \ \mathcal V_{\text{cand}}=\operatorname{top-}k_{w\in\mathcal V}\big[w_{\text{in}}^{\top}\nabla\log p(y\mid x_{\text{prompt}})\big]\ \text{(gradient w.r.t. the embedding of }x^{(j)}_{\text{trig}}),\ \text{keep the candidate with the highest }p(y\mid\cdot);\ \text{LM frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{continuous parameters};\ \ell\ \text{discrete token choices (search space }|\mathcal V|^{\ell})\ \text{plus label-token sets }\mathcal V_y
methods.locus: input token sequence (trigger tokens placed by a template around the input and the [MASK] slot)
methods.structure: A discrete prompt: the prompt matrix is constrained to the vocabulary lattice \{E_w\}^{\ell}\subset\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d} and optimized by first-order (HotFlip-style) coordinate swaps; prompt tuning is the continuous relaxation of this set.
methods.mergeable_reason: The trigger tokens lengthen every input, so inference is not at the original cost (though no new parameters exist).
methods.identity_at_init: Triggers start as [MASK] tokens; there is no identity guarantee, since the template itself changes the input.
methods.key_idea: Turn a task into masked-LM cloze form and search for a few shared discrete trigger tokens (and label words) with gradient-ranked candidate swaps, eliciting knowledge from a frozen MLM without any fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Without fine-tuning, AutoPrompt-prompted RoBERTa-large reached 91.4% on SST-2; on LAMA fact retrieval, AutoPrompt prompts for BERT reached 43.3% precision@1 (7 trigger tokens) vs 34.1% for the best prior single prompt (LPAQA Top1).

relations.note: AutoPrompt restricts the soft prompt to rows of the embedding matrix; prompt tuning is its continuous relaxation
WARP replaced the discrete search with continuous prompt and verbalizer embeddings
continuous-prompt successor evaluated on the same LAMA probing setup
both tune only the prompt of a frozen LM; AutoPrompt needs gradients, BBT is derivative-free

corrections: results_note: the 43.3% LAMA P@1 is for BERT, not RoBERTa (Table 4; RoBERTa is weaker on LAMA)
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2010.15980 (Taylor Shin, 2020-10) confirmed; EMNLP 2020 confirmed via ACL Anthology 2020.emnlp-main.346. Eqs. 1-2: p(y|x_prompt) marginalized over V_y, triggers initialized to [MASK], V_cand = top-k[w_in^T grad log p(y|x_prompt)] confirmed. SST-2 91.4 (RoBERTa) confirmed. Not in HF PEFT.

papers.title: Understanding intermediate layers using linear classifier probes
papers.claim: Linear classifiers ('probes') trained independently on each layer's frozen features measure how linearly separable the representation is; on Inception v3 and ResNet-50 separability increases monotonically with depth.
papers.relevance: Names and formalizes the probe, the terminal object of selective PEFT (train only a linear map on frozen features) and the standard yardstick that every other adaptation method is compared against.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1610.01644 (Alain, 2016-10) confirmed; ICLR 2017 Workshop confirmed via OpenReview (ICLR.cc/2017/workshop submission; DBLP conf/iclr/AlainB17). Claim matches the abstract (Inception v3, ResNet-50, monotone separability).

papers.title: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
papers.claim: Networks become stable to SGD noise early in training: copies trained from a shared checkpoint end in a linearly connected region of low loss.
papers.relevance: Explains why weight-space interpolation and arithmetic (WiSE-FT, model soups, task arithmetic, slider composition) work when all models share a pre-trained starting point, i.e. why the 'affine structure' over W_0 is meaningful.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1912.05671 (Frankle, 2019-12; comment 'Published in ICML 2020') confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: DExperts: Decoding-Time Controlled Text Generation with Experts and Anti-Experts
papers.claim: Combining a pretrained LM with expert and anti-expert LMs in a product of experts (adding and subtracting logits) controls attributes such as toxicity and sentiment, and works with small (anti-)experts, even on GPT-3.
papers.relevance: The output-space composition rule that proxy-tuning and EFT reuse for adaptation: tuning as a translation of logits.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2105.03023 (Alisa Liu, 2021-05; comment 'ACL 2021 camera-ready') and ACL Anthology 2021.acl-long.522 confirmed; claim (product of experts, small (anti-)experts, GPT-3) matches the abstract.

papers.title: Universal Adversarial Triggers for Attacking and Analyzing NLP
papers.claim: A gradient-guided search over tokens finds short input-agnostic trigger sequences that force a target prediction for any input, and these triggers transfer across models.
papers.relevance: The discrete-token search that AutoPrompt adapts from attacks to task prompting; the 'hard prompt' end of the prompt family.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1908.07125 (Wallace, 2019-08; comment 'EMNLP 2019') and ACL Anthology D19-1221 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: FedPETuning: When Federated Learning Meets the Parameter-Efficient Tuning Methods of Pre-trained Language Models
papers.claim: A holistic empirical study of PEFT methods (adapters, prefix tuning, LoRA, BitFit) under federated learning: tuning and aggregating only lightweight parameters cuts communication greatly while keeping acceptable performance across heterogeneity levels, data scales and FL scenarios.
papers.relevance: Establishes federated PEFT as a setting where the adapter is the unit of communication and aggregation, which is where the algebraic issue of averaging factored updates (FFA-LoRA, FLoRA) arises.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2212.10025 (Zhuo Zhang, 2022-12) confirmed; the arXiv title is 'When Federated Learning Meets Pre-trained Language Models' Parameter-Efficient Tuning Methods', the Findings of ACL 2023 title (used here) is confirmed at ACL Anthology 2023.findings-acl.632. Adapter, prefix tuning, LoRA and BitFit are the PEFT methods studied.

papers.title: Towards Building the Federated GPT: Federated Instruction Tuning
papers.claim: Introduces Federated Instruction Tuning (FedIT) for LLMs, combining LoRA with FedAvg so that clients tune and upload only LoRA modules, which the server averages.
papers.relevance: The baseline whose separate averaging of A and B produces the cross-term aggregation error that FFA-LoRA and FLoRA correct.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.05644 (Jianyi Zhang, 2023-05) confirmed; ICASSP 2024 confirmed via Semantic Scholar/DBLP (conf/icassp). The paper adopts LoRA in the FedAvg framework (Sec. 3).

papers.title: Group Diffusion Transformers are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
papers.claim: Recasting visual generation tasks as generating a group of related images, by concatenating self-attention tokens across images in a DiT, enables task-agnostic zero-shot generation over 200 instructions in 30 tasks.
papers.relevance: The precursor that IC-LoRA simplifies: it shows that cross-image attention inside one DiT can carry task conditioning, which IC-LoRA then activates with a small LoRA instead of large-scale training.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.15027 (Lianghua Huang, 2024-10) confirmed; no peer-reviewed venue found (Semantic Scholar lists arXiv), so venue stays arXiv. '200 instructions across 30 tasks' matches the abstract.

notes: All 8 requested methods exist and are not duplicates; Linear probing / LP-FT is split into two entries (linear-probing, lp-ft). Three additions: EFT (eft), the concurrent twin of proxy-tuning with an identical per-token rule; FLoRA (flora-federated), the heterogeneous-rank federated method named in the brief; and HetLoRA (hetlora, EMNLP 2024), the zero-padding baseline FLoRA compares against. Naming: 'FLoRA' now names four methods in the catalog (flora-batched, flora-opt, flora-tucker, flora-federated); the slug disambiguates. linear-probing has no single originating paper. It is attributed to DeCAF (ICML 2014) as the canonical 'frozen deep features + linear classifier' transfer paper, and Alain & Bengio's probes are listed under papers; confidence is medium for this attribution. TinyTL's NeurIPS title ('Reduce Memory, Not Parameters') differs from its arXiv title ('Reduce Activations, Not Trainable Parameters'); the NeurIPS title is used. IC-LoRA is an arXiv tech report with qualitative results only. No official code was found for FFA-LoRA, EFT or HetLoRA. None of these methods is in HF PEFT as a named config. Concept Sliders and IC-LoRA produce plain LoRA weights loadable with LoraConfig/diffusers, but their training recipes are not in PEFT. FFA-LoRA can be emulated by freezing lora_A; PEFT ships LoRA-FA only as an optimizer. Cross-file suggestions: icedit (frontier.json) should get builds-on -> ic-lora, since ICEdit reuses the IC-LoRA diptych/in-context format; model-soups should get builds-on -> wise-ft. Web search budget was exhausted, so venues were checked through arXiv comments, OpenReview API, ACL Anthology, PMLR and official READMEs: Concept Sliders ECCV 2024, FLoRA NeurIPS 2024, EFT ICLR 2024, HetLoRA EMNLP 2024 and FedIT ICASSP 2024 were confirmed through OpenReview/DBLP records.
verification_summary: Adversarial check on 2026-10-01 of all 12 methods and 7 papers in gap-3. Metadata: all 19 arXiv ids were fetched in one export-API batch; titles, first authors and first-version years match. Two arXiv titles differ from venue titles and the venue titles are kept: TinyTL (NeurIPS 2020 proceedings) and FedPETuning (Findings of ACL 2023). Venues were confirmed via arXiv comments (Proxy-Tuning COLM 2024, WiSE-FT CVPR 2022, LP-FT ICLR 2022 oral, FFA-LoRA ICLR 2024, TinyTL NeurIPS 2020, DExperts, UAT, LMC), Crossref (Concept Sliders ECCV 2024, LNCS), OpenReview (EFT ICLR 2024 poster, Alain & Bengio ICLR 2017 Workshop), the NeurIPS proceedings (FLoRA 2024, TinyTL 2020), PMLR v32 (DeCAF ICML 2014), ACL Anthology (AutoPrompt, HetLoRA EMNLP 2024 main, FedPETuning, DExperts, UAT) and Semantic Scholar/DBLP (FedIT ICASSP 2024). IC-LoRA and GDT stay arXiv. Formulas were checked against the arXiv full text of every method paper plus the official configs for Concept Sliders and IC-LoRA. Fixes: IC-LoRA uses r = alpha = 16 and the flow-matching loss with frozen text encoders; the Concept Sliders code scale (rank 4, alpha 1) was added; LP-FT's phi^2 takes an absolute value; AutoPrompt's 43.3% LAMA P@1 is for BERT, not RoBERTa; FLoRA and HetLoRA adapt self-attention layers only; HetLoRA's B = 0 start is not stated in the paper; EFT's 70% figure is on a 0 (small FT) to 1 (large FT) scale; the FLoRA repo moved to ziyaow1010/FederatedLLM. HF PEFT (main 85be3f3, v0.21.1): WiSE-FT is now hf_peft = true via peft.helpers.rescale_adapter_scale, whose docstring states equivalence to WiSE-FT for LoRA with multiplier in [0,1]; no other gap-3 method has a PEFT config or helper. Mergeability and identity flags were unchanged. Relations: ffa-lora -> lora-fa and ffa-lora -> asylora were retyped from equivalent-to to competes-with, matching lora-fa <-> asylora; hetlora -> adalora was removed as unjustified; notes were sharpened for wise-ft -> linear-probing, linear-probing -> surgical-fine-tuning and ffa-lora -> flora-federated. All relation targets are kebab-case slugs that exist in some family file. Nothing was dropped. 20 field-level corrections in total.
